messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: SURPASS-CVOT randomized 13,299 adults with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease to Mounjaro (tirzepatide, up to 15 mg once weekly) or dulaglutide 1.5 mg once weekly, a GLP-1 medicine already approved to reduce cardiovascular risk, with a median follow-up of about 4 years.
- Cardiovascular death, non-fatal heart attack, or non-fatal stroke occurred in 12.1% of those taking Mounjaro compared with 13.0% of those taking dulaglutide (HR 0.92, 95.3% CI 0.83–1.01), meeting the trial's goal of non-inferiority but not demonstrating superiority.
- Death from any cause occurred in 8.5% of the Mounjaro group versus 10.1% of the dulaglutide group (HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.75–0.94), though this was not a primary endpoint and was not adjusted for multiple comparisons, so it should be read as exploratory.
Because the comparator was an active medicine rather than placebo, these results describe how Mounjaro performs against another GLP-1, not how much it lowers risk compared with no treatment.
Triples: [["SURPASS-CVOT", "studied", "13,299 adults with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease"], ["SURPASS-CVOT", "compared", "Mounjaro"], ["SURPASS-CVOT", "compared", "dulaglutide 1.5 mg once weekly"], ["Mounjaro", "has generic name", "tirzepatide"], ["Mounjaro", "has dosage form", "once weekly"], ["Mounjaro", "has maximum dose", "15 mg"], ["dulaglutide 1.5 mg once weekly", "is a", "GLP-1 medicine"], ["dulaglutide 1.5 mg once weekly", "approved to", "reduce cardiovascular risk"], ["SURPASS-CVOT", "had median follow up", "about 4 years"], ["Mounjaro", "had cardiovascular event rate", "12.1%"], ["dulaglutide 1.5 mg once weekly", "had cardiovascular event rate", "13.0%"], ["Mounjaro", "had hazard ratio", "0.92"], ["Mounjaro", "had confidence interval", "0.83–1.01"], ["SURPASS-CVOT", "demonstrated", "non-inferiority"], ["SURPASS-CVOT", "did not demonstrate", "superiority"], ["Mounjaro", "had all cause death rate", "8.5%"], ["dulaglutide 1.5 mg once weekly", "had all cause death rate", "10.1%"], ["Mounjaro", "had hazard ratio for all cause death", "0.84"], ["Mounjaro", "had confidence interval for all cause death", "0.75–0.94"], ["SURPASS-CVOT", "noted", "exploratory result"], ["SURPASS-CVOT", "used", "active comparator"], ["SURPASS-CVOT", "not compared to", "placebo"], ["SURPASS-CVOT", "compared", "another GLP-1 medicine"], ["SURPASS-CVOT", "did not measure", "risk reduction compared with no treatment"]]
Relations: ["approved to", "compared", "demonstrated", "did not demonstrate", "did not measure", "had all cause death rate", "had cardiovascular event rate", "had confidence interval", "had confidence interval for all cause death", "had hazard ratio", "had hazard ratio for all cause death", "had median follow up", "has dosage form", "has generic name", "has maximum dose", "is a", "not compared to", "noted", "studied", "used"]
Answer:

completion:
approved to: The subject entity is approved for the medical purpose or indication specified by the object entity.  
compared: The subject study or drug was compared to the object entity in a clinical trial or analysis.  
demonstrated: The subject study showed or proved the outcome or result specified by the object entity.  
did not demonstrate: The subject study failed to show or prove the outcome or result specified by the object entity.  
did not measure: The subject study did not assess or evaluate the outcome or result specified by the object entity.  
had all cause death rate: The subject drug or treatment was associated with the specified percentage of all-cause mortality.  
had cardiovascular event rate: The subject drug or treatment was associated with the specified percentage of cardiovascular events.  
had confidence interval: The subject result or measurement had the specified range of statistical uncertainty.  
had confidence interval for all cause death: The subject result or measurement of all-cause mortality had the specified range of statistical uncertainty.  
had hazard ratio: The subject result or measurement had the specified relative risk compared to a comparator.  
had hazard ratio for all cause death: The subject result or measurement of all-cause mortality had the specified relative risk compared to a comparator.  
had median follow up: The subject study had the specified duration of follow-up for participants.  
has dosage form: The subject drug is administered in the specified pharmaceutical form.  
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.  
has maximum dose: The subject drug has the specified maximum dose strength.  
is a: The subject entity is classified as or belongs to the category specified by the object entity.  
not compared to: The subject study did not compare the drug or treatment to the object entity.  
noted: The subject study identified or highlighted the specified finding or observation.  
studied: The subject study investigated or analyzed the specified population or condition.  
used: The subject study utilized or employed the specified method or comparator.
